Prem Singh Yadav *
Division of Animal Physiology and Reproduction, ICAR, Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes (CIRB), India
Led the ICAR-CIRB research team that achieved the historic production of seven cloned calves from a single superior Murrah breeding bull named M-29 between October 2019 and January 2020
Recognized by ICAR for producing eight cloned buffalo calves (seven M-29 clones and one re-cloned Hisar-Gaurav calf) to multiply elite breeding bull germplasm across India

Inducted into the Limca Book of Records and India Book of Records for the national record of producing most cloned calves (7 clones) from a single superior Murrah breeding bull M-29 and re-cloning Hisar-Gaurav at ICAR-CIRB
Conferred the prestigious SAPI Fellow Award (FSAPI) by the Society of Animal Physiologists of India for scientific contributions to animal biotechnology and reproductive physiology
Co-editor of the book compendium "Buffalo Production Using Reproductive Biotechnology", published by ICAR-CIRB for ASEAN country scientific training
Co-discoverer of Murrah bull male fertility genetic variants deposited in GenBank (Accession Nos. KU364415, KU364416, KX463461, KX463462)
Pioneered piggyBac and transposon-mediated somatic cell reprogramming to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) in buffaloes
Led research on somatic cell cryobanking for indefinite viable preservation of the whole genome of elite Indian buffaloes
Received Best Research Paper Presentation Award at the XXXII Annual Convention of ISSAR (Tirupati, Dec 2016) for seminal plasma antioxidant markers in bull fertility

Reported in The Tribune India (Hisar Edition) as Project Head for proving the fertility and commercial breeding viability of cloned Murrah bull Hisar Gaurav through artificial insemination in field trials

Superannuated as Principal Scientist and Head of Division (Animal Physiology and Reproduction) from ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes (CIRB), Hisar after decades of pioneering buffalo cloning research
Principal Investigator for the 2022–2025 NASF Phase-II national project evaluating long-term health, semen characteristics, and fertility parameters of cloned buffalo progenies across India
Pioneered non-invasive donor cell isolation from semen-derived epithelial cells for somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) buffalo cloning in 2025
Earned B.Sc. in Agriculture & Animal Sciences from CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar in 1985
Earned M.Sc. in Animal Biotechnology / Physiology from CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar in 1987
Earned Ph.D. in Reproductive Physiology & Animal Biotechnology from CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar in 1991
Served as Lead International Scientific Trainer for ASEAN country delegates in advanced buffalo reproductive biotechnology and somatic cell nuclear transfer

Delivered invited scientific presentations on induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and buffalo cloning at the 7th International Conference on Stem Cells and Cancer (ICSCC 2016) and ISSRF 2017 (AIIMS New Delhi)
Principal Investigator for the ICAR national research project "Large scale production of multiple copies of elite buffalo bulls using animal cloning technology" (2018–2022)
Authored "Successful cloning of a superior buffalo bull", published in Nature Scientific Reports (Scientific Reports 9: 11366, doi:10.1038/s41598-019-47909-8)
Authored over 50 indexed biomedical research publications in NCBI PubMed database on somatic cell nuclear transfer, germplasm cryopreservation, and reproductive physiology

{{Draft article}}
{{Short description|Animal cloning researcher}}

'''Prem Singh Yadav''' is an Indian scientist whose research focuses on buffalo cloning<ref name="src-d03b0f5819">{{cite web|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/cibr-scientists-clone-7-elite-m-29-buffaloes-re-clone-one-5561561.html|title=CIBR scientists clone 7 elite M-29 buffaloes, re-clone one|website=Moneycontrol|date=2020-07-17}}</ref>.
In 2020, Moneycontrol identified Yadav as head of the CIRB cloning team<ref name="src-d03b0f5819" />.

==Education==
A publisher biography for Yadav’s book states that he graduated from the College of Agriculture, HAU, in 1985 and obtained an M.Sc. in 1987 and Ph.D. in 1991 from the Department of Animal Production Physiology, College of Animal Sciences, CCSHAU<ref name="src-cb4d0938de">{{cite web|url=https://www.bagchee.com/books/BB60406/reproductive-biotechnology-in-buffalo|title=Reproductive Biotechnology in Buffalo|website=Bagchee book catalogue}}</ref>.

==Career==
The 2023 ICAR-CIRB staff list recorded Yadav as a principal scientist with a joining date of 12 April 1993<ref name="src-e73557644a">{{cite web|url=https://cirb.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Staff-Remuneration-List-Hisar-2023.pdf|title=Scientists Remunerations|website=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes|date=2023}}</ref>. As a senior scientist at ICAR-CIRB, Yadav began a 12-month Department of Biotechnology Overseas Associateship in Neustadt, Germany, on 15 November 2003<ref name="src-75cd616383">{{cite web|url=https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/PARTNERSHIP-AND-LINKAGES-02_0.pdf|title=ICAR Partnership and Linkages: Overseas training during 2003–04|website=Indian Council of Agricultural Research|date=2003}}</ref>. An archived official ICAR-CIRB profile records that Yadav received DAAD Research support in 2010<ref name="src-87ac8ccc96">{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723192859/https://cirb.icar.gov.in/ps-yadav/|title=Dr. Prem Singh Yadav|website=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes (archived official profile)|date=23 July 2021}}</ref>. ICAR-CIRB’s 2010–11 annual report records Yadav’s research stay at Farm Animal Genetics, Germany, from 28 December 2010 to 10 February 2011<ref name="src-4fdcf94f36">{{cite web|url=https://cirb.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/annualreport2010-2011.pdf|title=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes Annual Report 2010–11|website=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes|date=2010–11}}</ref>. In 2018, The Tribune identified Yadav as a principal scientist and project head at ICAR-CIRB<ref name="src-12f91675f5">{{cite web|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/haryana/cloned-bull-s-semen-used-to-produce-20-calves-in-8-months-698521/|title=Cloned bull's semen used to produce 20 calves in 8 months|website=The Tribune|date=14 December 2018}}</ref>. In 2022, a PTI report described him as principal investigator of the Hisar Gaurav cloning project<ref name="src-5371d6d304">{{cite web|url=https://theprint.in/india/hisar-gaurav-first-cloned-calf-born-at-icar-cirb-turns-7/1260625/|title='Hisar Gaurav', first cloned calf born at ICAR-CIRB, turns 7|website=theprint.in}}</ref>. ICAR-CIRB's 2024 annual report listed Yadav as a principal scientist<ref name="src-aeb6d915a9">{{cite web|url=https://cirb.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/CIRB_AR_2024.pdf|title=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes Annual Report 2024|website=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes|date=2024}}</ref>. Yadav retired as an ICAR-CIRB principal scientist in 2025<ref name="src-30cdb84a23">{{cite web|url=https://www.amarujala.com/haryana/rewari/principal-scientist-dr-prem-singh-retired-rewari-news-c-198-1-rew1001-218880-2025-05-03|title=प्रधान वैज्ञानिक डॉ. प्रेम सिंह हुए सेवानिवृत्त|website=Amar Ujala|date=3 May 2025}}</ref>.

==Research==
ICAR reported that a team led by Yadav produced the cloned Murrah bull Hisar Gaurav in 2015<ref name="src-443a3f8b23">{{cite web|url=https://icar.gov.in/node/4887|title=ICAR-CIRB become India’s second center to produce cloned buffalo {{!}} ICAR|website=icar.gov.in}}</ref>. NDTV reported that the CIRB team headed by Yadav produced the cloned Assamese buffalo Sach-Gaurav in December 2017<ref name="src-b4ab04664d">{{cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/indias-first-cloned-assamese-buffalo-born-1824454|title=India’s First Cloned Assamese Buffalo Born|website=NDTV|date=15 March 2018}}</ref>. The Times of India reported that the Hisar Gaurav cloning team worked under Yadav's leadership<ref name="src-89f4cef816">{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/gurgaon/clone-murrah-buffalo-hisar-gaurav-turns-three-has-produced-20-male-and-female-calves/articleshow/67084199.cms|title=1st clone male Murrah buffalo turns 3|website=The Times of India|date=2018-12-14}}</ref>. Moneycontrol reported in 2020 that the CIRB team had cloned seven M-29 buffaloes and recloned Hisar Gaurav<ref name="src-d03b0f5819" />. Amar Ujala reported in 2020 that Yadav was chief scientist of the project that produced seven M-29 clones and one re-clone<ref name="src-edb32eef83">{{cite web|url=https://www.amarujala.com/haryana/hisar/cirb-hisar-has-created-seven-cloned-pieces-one-re-clone-hisar-news-rtk5643533104|title=सीआईआरबी हिसार ने तैयार किए सात क्लोन कटड़े, एक री-क्लोन भी बनाया|website=Amar Ujala|date=17 July 2020}}</ref>. Business Standard reported in 2021 that Yadav described efforts to demonstrate cloning’s use in multiplying proven buffalo bulls for breeding<ref name="src-1a851e9be8">{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/opinion/cloning-overcomes-prejudices-121072600018_1.html|title=Cloning overcomes prejudices|website=Business Standard|date=26 July 2021}}</ref>.

==Selected publications==
* Yadav was first author of "Evaluation of postnatal growth, hematology, telomere length and semen attributes of multiple clones and re-clone of superior buffalo breeding bulls", published in Theriogenology in 2024<ref name="src-f264a3ee95">{{cite web|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37793222/|title=Evaluation of postnatal growth, hematology, telomere length and semen attributes of multiple clones and re-clone of superior buffalo breeding bulls|website=PubMed|date=1 January 2024}}</ref>.
* Yadav co-authored "Production of MSTN Gene-Edited Embryos of Buffalo Using the CRISPR/Cas9 System and SCNT", published in Cellular Reprogramming<ref name="src-65e0c463e0">{{cite web|url=https://doi.org/10.1089/cell.2023.0003|title=Production of MSTN Gene-Edited Embryos of Buffalo Using the CRISPR/Cas9 System and SCNT|website=Cellular Reprogramming|date=2023}}</ref>.
* Yadav co-authored "Pluripotent Stem Cells for Livestock Health and Production.", published in Current Stem Cell Research & Therapy<ref name="src-79fe5f05a9">{{cite web|url=https://doi.org/10.2174/1574888X16666210803162019|title=Pluripotent Stem Cells for Livestock Health and Production.|website=Current Stem Cell Research & Therapy|date=2021}}</ref>.
* Yadav co-authored "Semen parameters and fertility potency of a cloned water buffalo bull produced from a semen-derived epithelial cell", published in PLOS ONE in 2020<ref name="src-a15f669816">{{cite web|url=https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0237766|title=Semen parameters and fertility potency of a cloned water buffalo bull produced from a semen-derived epithelial cell|website=PLOS ONE|date=21 August 2020}}</ref>.
* Yadav co-authored "Successful cloning of a superior buffalo bull", published in Scientific Reports in 2019<ref name="src-9c0f3d0c0c">{{cite web|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-47909-8|title=Successful cloning of a superior buffalo bull|website=Scientific Reports|date=6 August 2019}}</ref>.
* Yadav co-authored the book “Reproductive Biotechnology in Buffalo” (ISBN 8189304801)<ref name="src-11b51d3d09">{{cite web|url=https://ndri.res.in/sites/default/files/2025-06/ASAP%20April-2025.pdf|title=List of Indian e-Books of ASAP Publication (2018-20)|website=ICAR-National Dairy Research Institute|date=April 2025}}</ref>.
* Yadav was first author of “Bovine ICM derived cells express the Oct4 ortholog”, published in Cellular Reprogramming in 2005<ref name="src-0c979bd135">{{cite web|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15973686/|title=Bovine ICM derived cells express the Oct4 ortholog|website=PubMed}}</ref>.

==Awards and recognition==
ICAR-CIRB reported that Yadav was presented with the SAPI Fellow 2015 award in December 2016<ref name="src-62ed1b164c">{{cite web|url=https://cirb.res.in/news/icar-cirb-scientists-awarded/|title=ICAR-CIRB Scientists Awarded - ICAR - Central Institute for ...|website=cirb.res.in}}</ref>. Yadav led the Animal and Fisheries Sciences team that received one of the two 2019 Nanaji Deshmukh ICAR interdisciplinary research awards; ICAR reported 12 eligible applications<ref name="src-4deaa5ee4f">{{cite web|url=https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-08/ICAR_Citations_final_2020_Low_0.pdf|title=ICAR Award 2019 Citations|website=Indian Council of Agricultural Research|date=2020}}</ref>. India Book of Records credited an ICAR-CIRB team led by Yadav with producing eight buffalo clones between October 2019 and January 2020<ref name="src-6d2bc96231">{{cite web|url=https://indiabookofrecords.in/maximum-buffalo-clones-produced/|title=Maximum buffalo clones produced|website=India Book of Records|date=2021-06-11}}</ref>. ICAR-CIRB’s 2022 annual report stated that buffalo-cloning work by a team including Yadav was recognized by Limca Book of Records for the most calves cloned from a single bull<ref name="src-82b2b0c154">{{cite web|url=https://cirb.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Annual-report-2022.pdf|title=ICAR-CIRB Annual Report 2022|website=ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes|date=2022}}</ref>. Amar Ujala reported in 2023 that CIRB was registered in the Limca Book of Records for the maximum number of clones produced from one bull<ref name="src-dc3c3cfdc3">{{cite web|url=https://www.amarujala.com/photo-gallery/haryana/hisar/cirb-registered-in-limca-book-for-maximum-clone-for-one-bull-2023-03-15|title=CIRB registered in Limca Book for maximum clone for one bull|website=Amar Ujala}}</ref>.
